title: 밥은커녕 물도 못 마셨어요: 커녕과 치고
objective: By the end, you can use N은/는커녕 and -기는커녕 to say that not even the smaller thing happened. You can also use N치고(는) to say that someone or something is different from what people usually expect.
summary: Learn two particles of contrast: 커녕 ("let alone A, not even B") and 치고 ("for an N, unlike what you would expect").

task.title: Use 커녕 and 치고
task.line: Read each sentence, decide which particle it needs, and write the correct form.

forms.when: After a noun ending in a consonant.
forms.means: Not even B, let alone A. A is the bigger thing you expected, and B is the smaller thing that also didn't happen.
forms.exampleMeaning: I couldn't even drink water, let alone eat a meal.

forms.when: After a noun ending in a vowel.
forms.means: Same meaning as 은커녕. The second part usually has 도 or 만 and a negative or worse result.
forms.exampleMeaning: Forget a bonus — even my salary came late.

forms.when: After a verb or adjective stem.
forms.means: The opposite or something worse happened instead.
forms.exampleMeaning: Far from stopping, the rain is getting heavier.

forms.when: Directly after a noun. 는 adds emphasis.
forms.means: For an N. The result is different from what people usually expect from N — it can be better or worse than expected.
forms.exampleMeaning: For a dish you made for the first time, it's really tasty.

forms.when: Directly after a noun. Without 는, it means the same thing, and it works for both better and worse results (봄 날씨치고는 꽤 춥네요 is also correct).
forms.means: For an N; different from what is usual for an N (better or worse).
forms.exampleMeaning: It's pretty cold for spring weather.

watchOut: 밥은커녕 물도 많이 마셨어요 (X) → 밥은커녕 물도 못 마셨어요 (O): After 커녕, the second part is negative or worse.
물은커녕 밥도 못 먹었어요 (X) → 밥은커녕 물도 못 먹었어요 (O): Put the bigger thing before 커녕 and the smaller thing before 도.
선물는커녕 (X) → 선물은커녕 (O): Use 은커녕 after a consonant and 는커녕 after a vowel.
외국 사람인치고 (X) → 외국 사람치고 (O): 치고 goes straight onto the noun, without 이다.
exercises: Fill in each blank with 은커녕 or 는커녕: ① 요즘 너무 바빠서 휴가____ 주말에도 일해요. ② 실수를 해서 칭찬____ 혼만 났어요.
Fill in each blank with 은/는커녕 or 치고(는): ① 이 가방은 싼 가방____ 품질이 좋아요. ② 저는 운전____ 자전거도 못 타요. ③ 초등학생____ 키가 정말 크네요.
Change the word in brackets to the -기는커녕 form: 약을 먹었는데 감기가 (낫다) ____ 더 심해졌어요.
Put the words in the right order to make one sentence, starting with 바빠서: 못 했어요 / 식사는커녕 / 바빠서 / 한 잔도 / 커피
Complete B's answer with N치고(는): 가: 회사 식당 음식 어때요? 나: 회사 ____ 꽤 맛있어요.
Complete B's answer with -기는커녕, using 조용하다: 가: 새로 이사한 집은 조용해요? 나: 아니요, ____ 밤마다 옆집이 시끄러워요.
answers: ① 치고(는) ② 은커녕 ③ 치고(는)
